description: Stable, non-sensitive reason codes a BEAP implementation emits. `category` groups them; `verdict` is the verdict the code accompanies when it decides an evaluation, `null` when it annotates a later lifecycle stage.

entries.description: Every authority requirement of the effective policy is satisfied.
A credit officer must approve the exact intent.
Two independent authorities must approve the exact intent.
A treasury authority must approve the exact intent.
A mandated signatory must approve the exact intent.
A checker distinct from the maker must approve the exact intent.
A verified human ceremony bound to the intent digest is required.
The matched rule escalates without naming a specific authority; policy-defined authority evidence is required.
No enabled rule of the effective policy matched the action; the evaluation fails safe.
A fact path the policy requires is absent; the evaluation fails safe.
A material signal or approval is older than the policy freshness window.
No effective policy could be resolved for the domain; the evaluation fails closed.
The execution authority could not be reached or returned an unusable response; fail closed.
The effective policy explicitly disallows the proposed action.
The subject's identity verification status does not permit the action.
A screening signal disallows the action.
The action type is not registered for the execution domain.
The proposed action does not conform to the canonical BankingAction schema.
A named compliance officer must approve the exact customer or account before it is created or activated.
The party's prior relationship and adverse findings could not be validated; a named reviewer must decide.
An approval binds a different intent digest than the action being authorized.
The same approver was counted twice for one requirement.
One approver satisfied two requirements that must be held by distinct persons.
An approval or the authority set expired before the binding was created.
An approval was offered for a role the authority set does not require.
The approval's evidence could not be verified.
The proposed action changed; collected approvals no longer bind it.
Intent capture refused an action whose Intent Digest is not the digest the presented AuthoritySet bound.
Intent capture refused an action whose presented AuthoritySet has not collected every required approval.
An approval was offered to a set that is no longer collecting (satisfied, bound, consumed, rejected, expired, or invalidated).
The intent digest recomputed at the execution boundary differs from the bound digest.
The execution grant's validity window has passed.
The single-use grant was already claimed or finalized.
The execution authority presented with the attempt is not valid for it: it was already consumed, has expired, or does not bind this intent.
The authority refused the claim; the downstream commit was not attempted.
The claim lease expired before the outcome was known; the attempt is finalized as INDETERMINATE.
The effective policy, a material signal, or the approval state changed between authorization and the claim; the grant is refused.
A monetary amount does not use the currency's minor-unit scale.
Authoritative downstream evidence differs materially from the authorized effect.
The executor cannot prove whether the protected effect occurred.
An outcome must be resolved through authoritative downstream identifiers before any further action.
Effect evidence could not be durably recorded for an execution that may have occurred.
Two batch items share an item reference.
The manifest digest recomputed from the items differs from the bound manifest digest.
The source file digest differs from the digest recorded in the manifest.
Manifest items are not in ascending byte order of item reference.
Per-currency totals are not in ascending byte order of currency code.
The declared totals do not reproduce from the manifest items.
An item digest does not reproduce from the item's canonical content.
The item count carried by the batch action differs from the manifest's item count.
A batch-releasing action carries no batch reference.
A batch-releasing action carries no aggregate amount and currency in its financial context.
An item outcome was reported for an item digest the authorized manifest does not contain.

A reconciliation report for a batch is not a usable observation: it carries no outcomes, an outcome that does not satisfy the item-outcome structure, or a provider-supplied field the evidence record cannot carry.
An item outcome contradicts an outcome already recorded as final for that item.
The manifest does not satisfy the Batch Manifest structure, so no binding can be derived from it.
